expectations.text: Imports and uses SPACING or SPACING_PATTERNS from @/config/spacing instead of arbitrary pixel values

Used extensively throughout: SPACING.base, SPACING.xs, SPACING.sm, SPACING.md, SPACING.lg, SPACING.xl, SPACING['2xl'], SPACING_PATTERNS.pagePadding, SPACING_PATTERNS.sectionGap, SPACING_PATTERNS.formFieldGap, SPACING_PATTERNS.buttonGroupGap, SPACING_PATTERNS.stackSpacing.

Line 30: `import { TYPOGRAPHY } from '@/helpers/typography'`. Used for TYPOGRAPHY.h1, h3, body, small, xs, label, bold, semibold, medium, normal throughout.

Lines 22-28: `import { TRANSITIONS, HOVER_EFFECTS, ACTIVE_EFFECTS, FOCUS_STYLES, MOTION_VARIANTS } from '@/config/transitions'`. claims.evidence: Line 239: `const activeNotificationCount = useMemo(...)` for computing active notification count.
IconButtons have aria-label='Copy wallet address' (line 513) and aria-label='View address on block explorer' (line 534). Custom slippage input has aria-label (line 615).

suggestions.reason: Consider also checking that NO arbitrary pixel/rem values appear alongside the constants. This output has 'w="80px"' on line 603 and border-radius strings like '16px' and '8px' throughout, which are not from SPACING constants. The assertion passes because it only checks for imports/usage, not for absence of violations.
No assertion checks for proper aria-labels on interactive elements (icon buttons, custom inputs). The with_skill output does include them, but this would not be caught if omitted.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the main design system requirements well. The spacing assertion could be strengthened to also check for absence of arbitrary values.
